literal: He who begs, not getting angry is required; the distress of poverty, even itself indeed, is sufficient witness.
translation: One who begs must not get angry when refused; the distress of his own poverty is itself a sufficient witness to his helpless state.
modern: இரப்பவர் பிறர் தமக்குக் கொடாவிட்டாலும் கோபிக்காமல் இருக்க வேண்டும்; அவருடைய வறுமைத் துன்பமே அதற்குப் போதுமான சான்றாகும்.
explanation: This couplet advises those who are forced to beg to maintain patience and avoid anger when they are turned away. The poet explains that the beggar's own state of poverty and the suffering it brings ('nirappu iṭumpai') serve as a sufficient witness ('kari') to their helplessness. Getting angry at others who do not give is pointless, as the beggar's own destitute condition already proves their lack of power or standing to demand anything. Thus, accepting one's situation without resentment is the only dignified path left.
